newsitem.title: USA: Mexico's Zedillo says not worried by peso drop.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo says not worried by peso drop.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zediilo said in an interview published Friday that he is not worried by the peso's sharp drop against the dollar in recent days.
"We are not concerned about exchange rates," Zedillo told the Dallas Morning News in a Mexico City interview. "What we have a commitment to are strong, disciplined fiscal and monetary policies."
The peso stood at around 7.95 to the dollar at midday Friday. That was down 2.9 percent from October 18 and 5.2 percent from September 27.
The peso collapsed shortly after Zedillo came to power in December 1994 and its fall pushed the economy into a deep recession last year.
But a stiff austerity program brought inflation down and the economy began recovering this year.
"We have made tremendous progress ... This is not a task we are going to complete overnight, but I think little by little we're doing the job," Zedillo told the Dallas Morning News.
He also scoffed at opposition claims that Mexicans' standard of living has dropped steadily in recent years.
"It's not true that Mexico is worse off today than it was 20 or 40 years ago," he said. "We were much poorer not so many years ago."
